Codex Ultra Integration and SLA Quick Reference

Friendly noteSA-VM does not support directly calling JavaScript or Python to perform system operations. Please do not generate node, python, bun, PowerShell, cmd, or shell commands to read/write files, run Git, or access the network; such requests will be rejected. When execution is needed, first read the examples on this page, then use sa_vm_run(language: "sla"); ordinary JS/Python code that is only for explanation or display may be output as text, but must not be executed directly.
First rule for the modelIn Codex Ultra SA-VM conversations, do not guess SLA syntax. First read this help page and the “SLA Language Reference”, then generate complete language: "sla" source code and call sa_vm_run. If you are unsure of a function signature, first check the corresponding standard library page; do not switch to the host shell instead.

1. Calling Convention

VM conversations may only execute automation through the dynamic tool sa_vm_run. A request uses language: "sla" and a complete source; file, network, environment variable, and process capabilities are declared minimally in requested_caps, and are checked a second time by the current conversation’s policy.

{
  "language": "sla",
  "source": "@import \\\"sa_std/io/print.sai\\\"\\n\\nfn main() -> i32 {\\n    println(\\\"hello from SLA\\\");\\n    return 0;\\n}",
  "requested_caps": { "fs": [] },
  "limits": { "deadline_ms": 5000 }
}
  • source must be a complete program, usually containing fn main() -> i32.
  • Strings are slice values; when passing them to a pointer parameter use STR_PTR(value), and for the length use STR_LEN(value).
  • extern functions generally return a status code: 0 means success, non-zero means failure.
  • Do not put JavaScript, Python, PowerShell, cmd, or shell strings into SLA; that is not SLA syntax.

2. Read the Help First, Then Write the Program

Before generating SLA, consult the offline documentation in the installation package in the following order:

  1. resources/sa-vm/sala/dist/index.html: open the help viewer.
  2. resources/sa-vm/sala/dist/content/12_vm/07_codex_ultra.html: this page, containing the Codex Ultra tool combinations.
  3. resources/sa-vm/sala/dist/content/02_sla_lang/: lexical structure, types, functions, ownership, modules.
  4. resources/sa-vm/sala/dist/content/06_stdlib/06_fs.html: filesystem signatures and macros.
  5. resources/sa-vm/sala/dist/content/06_stdlib/09_process.html: the argv process API.

The recommended approach is to copy a complete example and only replace the paths, parameters, and capabilities; if a help file is missing, report the absence — do not invent an API yourself.

3. Reading Files

3.1 Reading Specified Lines (Most Common)

@import "sa_std/fs.sai"
@import "sa_std/string.sa"

fn main() -> i32 {
    let path = "E:/workspace/src/main.ts";
    return sa_fs_read_lines_to_stdout(
        STR_PTR(path), STR_LEN(path),
        1, 120, 65536
    );
}
"requested_caps": {
  "fs": [{ "op": "read", "path": "E:/workspace/src/main.ts" }]
}

Line numbers are 1-based and inclusive of both ends; start_line == 0 or end_line < start_line will fail.

3.2 Searching for File Names

@import "sa_std/fs.sai"
@import "sa_std/string.sa"

fn main() -> i32 {
    let root = "E:/workspace";
    let pattern = "*.ts";
    return sa_fs_find_files_to_stdout(
        STR_PTR(root), STR_LEN(root),
        STR_PTR(pattern), STR_LEN(pattern),
        200, 6
    );
}
"requested_caps": {
  "fs": [{ "op": "read", "path": "E:/workspace" }]
}

Searching is only performed within root directories that are allowed to be read; always set a finite max_entries and max_depth.

3.3 Reading Metadata

@import "sa_std/fs.sai"
@import "sa_std/string.sa"

fn main() -> i32 {
    let path = "E:/workspace/package.json";
    let metadata = sa_fs_metadata(STR_PTR(path), STR_LEN(path));
    if metadata == 0 { return 1; }
    let size = sa_fs_metadata_len(metadata);
    println("bytes={}", size);
    return sa_fs_metadata_free(metadata);
}

A metadata request declares { "op": "metadata", "path": "..." }; an owned metadata handle must call sa_fs_metadata_free.

3.4 Reading a Complete File and Releasing the Handle

@import "sa_std/fs.sai"
@import "sa_std/string.sa"

fn main() -> i32 {
    let path = "E:/workspace/data.json";
    let buffer = sa_fs_read_file(STR_PTR(path), STR_LEN(path), 1048576);
    if buffer == 0 { return 1; }
    let length = sa_fs_read_buffer_len(buffer);
    println("read={}", length);
    return sa_fs_read_buffer_free(^buffer);
}

A whole-file read must set max_bytes, and must release the owned buffer on all success paths; otherwise a VM handle leak will occur.

3.5 Relative Paths (Recommended, Reduces Repeated Tokens)

File and directory paths may be written relative to the workspace confirmed for the current conversation (the VM’s cwd). The broker automatically joins and normalizes relative paths at capability-check time; . denotes the workspace root, and .. cannot escape the root allowed by the policy. Relative paths in SLA source code are also resolved by the VM process with that workspace as the current directory.

@import "sa_std/fs.sai"
@import "sa_std/string.sa"

fn main() -> i32 {
    let path = "src/main.ts";
    let generated = "generated/report.txt";
    let first = sa_fs_read_lines_to_stdout(STR_PTR(path), STR_LEN(path), 1, 80, 32768);
    if first != 0 { return first; }
    return sa_fs_write_file(STR_PTR(generated), STR_LEN(generated), STR_PTR("status = ready\n"), 15);
}
"requested_caps": {
  "fs": [
    { "op": "read", "path": "src" },
    { "op": "read", "path": "src/main.ts" },
    { "op": "write", "path": "generated/report.txt" }
  ]
}
  • For directory reads/searches use a directory relative path, e.g. src, tests/fixtures; directory creation uses create, file overwrite writes use write.
  • Every source and target of a read, write, copy, or move is still checked separately; relative paths do not loosen the policy.
  • Do not repeatedly write full drive-letter paths in the same request; only use an absolute path or an explicit root path for an approved additional root outside the workspace.

4. Writing, Appending, and Atomic Editing

4.1 Overwrite Write

@import "sa_std/fs.sai"
@import "sa_std/string.sa"

fn main() -> i32 {
    let path = "E:/workspace/out.txt";
    let data = "generated by SLA\n";
    return sa_fs_write_file(
        STR_PTR(path), STR_LEN(path),
        STR_PTR(data), STR_LEN(data)
    );
}
"requested_caps": {
  "fs": [{ "op": "write", "path": "E:/workspace/out.txt" }]
}

4.2 Appending a Log

@import "sa_std/fs.sai"
@import "sa_std/string.sa"

fn main() -> i32 {
    let path = "E:/workspace/logs/run.log";
    let line = "step complete\n";
    return sa_fs_append_file(
        STR_PTR(path), STR_LEN(path),
        STR_PTR(line), STR_LEN(line)
    );
}

An append declares { "op": "append", "path": "E:/workspace/logs/run.log" }; do not simulate appending with an overwrite write.

4.3 Read–Match–Atomic Replace

@import "sa_std/fs.sai"
@import "sa_std/string.sa"

fn main() -> i32 {
    let path = "E:/workspace/config.toml";
    let old_text = "debug = false";
    let new_text = "debug = true";
    return sa_fs_edit_file(
        STR_PTR(path), STR_LEN(path),
        STR_PTR(old_text), STR_LEN(old_text),
        STR_PTR(new_text), STR_LEN(new_text),
        -1, 0
    );
}
  • expected_mtime_ms = -1: use when there is no snapshot; when there is a snapshot, pass the real mtime to enable CAS.
  • replace_all = 0: requires exactly one match; only use 1 when all occurrences need to be replaced.
  • The helper rejects stale mtimes and ambiguous matches, and preserves the UTF-8/BOM/UTF-16 and CRLF style.

5. Directories, Copying, Moving, and Deleting

5.1 Create a Directory, Then Write a File

@import "sa_std/fs.sai"
@import "sa_std/string.sa"

fn main() -> i32 {
    let directory = "E:/workspace/generated/reports";
    let path = "E:/workspace/generated/reports/summary.txt";
    let data = "report\n";
    let status = sa_fs_make_dir(STR_PTR(directory), STR_LEN(directory));
    if status != 0 { return status; }
    return sa_fs_write_file(STR_PTR(path), STR_LEN(path), STR_PTR(data), STR_LEN(data));
}

Directory creation declares op: "create"; a file write still needs its own op: "write" declaration.

5.2 Copying a File

@import "sa_std/fs.sai"
@import "sa_std/string.sa"

fn main() -> i32 {
    let source = "E:/workspace/input.json";
    let destination = "E:/workspace/backup/input.json";
    return sa_fs_copy_file(
        STR_PTR(source), STR_LEN(source),
        STR_PTR(destination), STR_LEN(destination)
    );
}

Copying requires both the source’s read capability and the target’s write capability; both sides must pass the policy.

5.3 Moving or Renaming

@import "sa_std/fs.sai"
@import "sa_std/string.sa"

fn main() -> i32 {
    let from = "E:/workspace/tmp.txt";
    let to = "E:/workspace/final.txt";
    return sa_fs_rename(
        STR_PTR(from), STR_LEN(from),
        STR_PTR(to), STR_LEN(to)
    );
}

Moving requires the source’s rename/transfer and the target’s rename/write. A move across thread roots is rejected.

5.4 Deleting

@import "sa_std/fs.sai"
@import "sa_std/string.sa"

fn main() -> i32 {
    let path = "E:/workspace/generated/old.txt";
    return sa_fs_remove_path(STR_PTR(path), STR_LEN(path));
}

Deletion is not unconditionally allowed: when the current conversation’s policy is delete: deny it will definitely fail; when the policy is rename/move, Codex Ultra’s apply_patch instead moves the file to backupDir. Do not use deletion to bypass the backup rules.

6. The Official apply_patch Combination

VM mode retains the official apply_patch tool. The model may submit a patch directly; do not wrap a patch in a shell or PowerShell command.

*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: src/new.ts
+export const enabled = true
*** Update File: src/config.ts
@@
-export const mode = "old"
+export const mode = "new"
*** Update File: src/legacy.ts
*** Move to: src/archive/legacy.ts
*** Delete File: src/obsolete.ts
*** End Patch

The broker will:

  1. Parse Add/Update/Delete/Move and multiple hunks;
  2. Check every read path, write path, delete source path, move source path, and target path;
  3. Convert the operations into sa_fs_write_file, sa_fs_edit_file, sa_fs_rename inside the VM;
  4. Return a structured result, without directly calling host file APIs.

When a patch is rejected, do not retry the same request. Fix the boundaries, hunks, or policy and then submit again; both native-command rejections and out-of-authority patch rejections are terminal.

7. Completing Multiple File Operations in One SLA Program

@import "sa_std/fs.sai"
@import "sa_std/string.sa"

fn main() -> i32 {
    let config = "E:/workspace/generated/config.txt";
    let report = "E:/workspace/generated/report.txt";
    let config_data = "mode = safe\n";
    let report_data = "status = ready\n";
    let first = sa_fs_write_file(STR_PTR(config), STR_LEN(config), STR_PTR(config_data), STR_LEN(config_data));
    if first != 0 { return first; }
    return sa_fs_write_file(STR_PTR(report), STR_LEN(report), STR_PTR(report_data), STR_LEN(report_data));
}
"requested_caps": {
  "fs": [
    { "op": "write", "path": "E:/workspace/generated/config.txt" },
    { "op": "write", "path": "E:/workspace/generated/report.txt" }
  ]
}

A multi-file task should be completed in a single VM invocation, declaring a complete but minimal capability set; do not switch to host commands for each file.

8. Parallel Tasks

Independent read-only tasks can be run in batch via parallel. Each task is still an independent SLA VM, and results are returned in input order.

{
  "parallel": [
    {
      "language": "sla",
      "source": "@import \\\"sa_std/fs.sai\\\"\\n@import \\\"sa_std/string.sa\\\"\\nfn main() -> i32 { let p = \\\"E:/workspace/a.ts\\\"; return sa_fs_read_lines_to_stdout(STR_PTR(p), STR_LEN(p), 1, 80, 32768); }",
      "requested_caps": { "fs": [{ "op": "read", "path": "E:/workspace/a.ts" }] }
    },
    {
      "language": "sla",
      "source": "@import \\\"sa_std/fs.sai\\\"\\n@import \\\"sa_std/string.sa\\\"\\nfn main() -> i32 { let p = \\\"E:/workspace/b.ts\\\"; return sa_fs_read_lines_to_stdout(STR_PTR(p), STR_LEN(p), 1, 80, 32768); }",
      "requested_caps": { "fs": [{ "op": "read", "path": "E:/workspace/b.ts" }] }
    }
  ],
  "concurrency": 2
}

parallel allows at most 32 tasks, concurrency at most 8; when there are write dependencies, do not parallelize — instead execute sequentially in a single SLA program.

9. Processes and Git

Process execution uses an argv array, not shell concatenation. You must declare requested_caps.process: true, and the executable and arguments must match the policy allowlist.

@import "sa_std/process.sai"

fn main() -> i32 {
    // 按“标准库 > process：子进程”中的 SaProcessArgv 示例构造 argv。
    // argv[0] = "git"，后续元素分别是 "status"、"--short"、"--branch"。
    // 使用 sa_std_process_exec_capture 获取退出码、stdout 和 stderr。
    return 0;
}
"requested_caps": { "process": true }
  • Do not call cmd /c, powershell -Command, bash -lc, or shell pipelines.
  • Git is still doubly restricted by the process executable/args allowlist and the workspace read/write policy.
  • Capture handles must be closed with sa_std_close or the corresponding close helper after use.

10. Environment Variables and HTTPS

  • Environment variables may only read names listed in the policy’s env.allow; do not request the entire environment.
  • Networking only allows HTTPS; the host, path, and method must match policy.http.allow; do not use HTTP, account passwords, or arbitrary URLs.
  • File, network, environment variable, and process capabilities should only declare the minimal set needed for the current task.

11. Common Combination Checklist

TaskSLA APIrequested_capsExtra requirements
View lines 1–100 of a filesa_fs_read_lines_to_stdoutreadLimit line count and byte count
Search source filessa_fs_find_files_to_stdoutRoot directory readLimit depth and entry count
Overwrite-write a filesa_fs_write_filewriteConfirm the target allows writing
Append a logsa_fs_append_fileappendDo not simulate shell redirection
Precisely edit textsa_fs_edit_fileread + write / editPrefer passing an mtime CAS
Copysa_fs_copy_fileSource read + target writeCheck both sides
Move/renamesa_fs_renameSource rename + target renameMust not cross roots
Deletesa_fs_remove_pathdeleteObey deny/rename/move
Execute Gitsa_std_process_exec_captureprocess: trueargv-only, no shell
Multiple read-only tasksparallel + SLADeclared independently per taskConcurrency limit 8
Complex multi-file patchOfficial apply_patchBroker expands automaticallyEvery path checked one by one

12. Failure Handling and Infinite-Loop Prevention

  • policy_invalid: fix the policy JSON schema.
  • capability_denied: narrow the capability or have the user modify the current conversation’s policy.
  • timeout, fuel_exhausted, mem_quota: reduce the task scale or adjust the explicit limits.
  • SymbolNotFound, unavailable: check the sidecar, plugin DLLs, sa_std, and Sala help resources in the installation package.
  • After a native command is rejected, do not switch languages, do not repeat the same request, and do not call host tools; rewrite it once into SLA.
  • After a patch is rejected, only fix the patch format or paths; do not put the patch into a shell.

Recommended workflowRead this page and the corresponding API page → copy a complete example → declare only the needed capabilities → call sa_vm_run once → check the structured result → if necessary, fix with new input rather than retrying the same rejected request.
